messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: sev2 runtime OOM spike detected in us-west-2 - multiple GPU pods restarting. Affected cluster: gpu-prod. Auto-created incident: https://redwood/in/INC-619876 (priority: high)

maria: seeing CUDA OOMs + container crashes on gpu-prod-17 and gpu-prod-19. Paging metrics show persistent KV cache growth over last 15m.

chen: logs show repeated failures: ```2026-03-17T18:12:41Z runtime[pid=2432]: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
2026-03-17T18:12:41Z allocator: pagefrag=0.82 free_pages=120 used_pages=690
2026-03-17T18:12:42Z runtime: killing container due to OOM```

indra: we pushed model v2.3.4 ~8m ago with larger batch heuristics; could be surge in prefix lengths + larger kv usage. Can we confirm rollout?

jordan: confirming v2.3.4 rollout at 18:04 UTC. I'm going to start routing a portion back to r-lite fallback and increase eviction aggressiveness. Executing: `redwoodctl routing set --model r-lite --percent 40`

ops_sre: recommend enabling cache-sweeper and lowering eviction threshold temporarily. Sweeper endpoint: `POST https://ops-api/sweeper/run?cluster=gpu-prod` - will trigger soft-evict of stale prefixes. Also suggest cordoning gpu-prod-17 and draining pods.

maria: customer impact: ~12% request errors (503/timeouts) reported by SRE dashboard. Latency tail increased to ~2s on token generation. CS team looped in.

jordan: reroute 40% traffic done. Triggered sweeper. Starting node drain on gpu-prod-17: `kubectl drain gpu-prod-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

oncall-bot: Incident INC-619876 updated: status=investigating, severity=sev2. Postmortem draft created at https://redwood/pm/INC-619876-draft

indra: immediate mitigations: 1) limit batch size: `policy set batch_max 1` 2) disable large prefetch heuristics in runtime 3) enable allocator compaction toggle (if available)

chen: heap profile captured from dying pod: `/tmp/heap-6198765432.pb`. Early analysis: paged-attention allocator fragmentation + KV cache entries pinned by long-running sessions. Free-list appears to not compact when page fragmentation exceeds ~65%. Suspect regression in commit 3f7a1b (allocator: skip compaction for large pages).

ops_sre: Mitigation checklist posted: - drain/replace affected nodes - restart runtime containers after sweeper run - roll back v2.3.4 if instability continues - deploy quick allocator toggle patch (compaction on) to canary 1 pod - monitor eviction rate (>200/s target) and RSS on pods

jordan: rolled back model rollout to r-stable in routing (r-lite fallback). Saw immediate reduction in OOMs on one node; others still noisy. Sweeper reduced RSS on two pods by ~3.6GB each.

maria: handing off active coordination to jordan for the next 2 hours. I'm going to update incident doc with notes and customer list. /me :thumbsup:

jordan: will continue monitoring metrics and run allocator patch canary in 10m. Notifying CS with support ticket #12345 and impacted customer list. If OOMs return after patch, we escalate to full allocator rollback.

indra: long-term action items logged: revert risky allocator change from 3f7a1b, add canary for compaction behavior, improve KV cache TTL heuristics on long-running sessions, add alert for pagefrag > 70% with sustained growth.

chen: attaching short snippet of the diagnostic command we used to profile pages: ```/opt/redwood/bin/alloc-prof --pid 2432 --dump-pages /tmp/pages-619876.txt```

ops_sre: note: kube node gpu-prod-17 drained and cordoned; pods rescheduled to gpu-prod-21/22. Sweeper run completed. Monitoring shows eviction_rate spike to 230/s and drop in pagefrag to ~0.58 on affected pods.

jordan: update 18:24 UTC - OOM events down to 0-1/m. Keeping routing at 60% r-stable / 40% r-lite until we verify allocator patch. I'll do a handoff to indra at 19:05 UTC for night coverage.

maria: thanks team, leaving incident notes in doc (https://redwood/pm/INC-619876-draft). I'll follow up on customer comms in the AM.

oncall-bot: Closing note: remember to annotate timelines in postmortem and capture heap dumps for next 24h.
